questions.title: Co-trimoxazole combines trimethoprim with sulfamethoxazole, not clavulanic acid
questions.question: All the following are true concerning co-trimoxazole EXCEPT:

options.A: It inhibits two sequential steps in the synthesis of tetrahydrofolic acid
options.B: It is the treatment of choice for dugs caused by pneumocystis cranii
options.C: It is a combination of Trimethoprim and clavulanic acid

explanations.A: Incorrect (as the EXCEPT) -- this statement is true. Sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim block two sequential steps of the same bacterial folate synthesis pathway, giving co-trimoxazole its synergistic effect.
explanations.B: Incorrect (as the EXCEPT) -- this statement is true. Co-trimoxazole is the treatment of choice for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia.
explanations.C: Correct (as the EXCEPT). Co-trimoxazole is a combination of trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole, not clavulanic acid -- clavulanic acid is instead a beta-lactamase inhibitor paired with amoxicillin (co-amoxiclav), an entirely different combination drug. This is the false statement among the options, since sulfamethoxazole, not clavulanic acid, is co-trimoxazole's actual second component.
explanations.D: Incorrect (as the EXCEPT) -- this statement is true. Skin rashes, including severe hypersensitivity reactions, are a recognised co-trimoxazole adverse effect.

questions.learning_objective: State that co-trimoxazole combines trimethoprim with sulfamethoxazole, not clavulanic acid.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: It is a combination of Trimethoprim and clavulanic acid"
